prompt:
Physicist Chien-Shiung Wu designed a careful experiment in 1956 that helped test a major idea about particle behavior. Her results challenged what many scientists had assumed and influenced later research in physics. Because of this impact, Wu’s work is often described as ______ in the history of modern science.
Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word?
explanation: The text describes Wu’s experiment as challenging assumptions and influencing later research, so “significant” is the most precise choice.

prompt:
Some school cafeterias have high ceilings and hard floors that cause sound to bounce around the room. When many students are talking at once, the noise can become distracting. Installing sound-absorbing panels on walls and ceilings can make the space quieter by reducing echoes.
Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

choices.A: Sound-absorbing panels can help reduce noise in school cafeterias.
choices.B: High ceilings are the only reason cafeterias become noisy.
choices.C: Students usually prefer cafeterias with hard floors.
choices.D: Echoes are useful because they help students hear conversations clearly.

explanation: The passage explains that panels reduce echoes and make noisy cafeterias quieter.

prompt:
A student recorded the number of seedlings that sprouted in four trays.
Tray | Number of seedlings sprouted
1 | 12
2 | 18
3 | 15
4 | 20
Which choice best describes the data in the table?

choices.A: Tray 4 had the greatest number of seedlings sprouted.
choices.B: Tray 1 and Tray 3 had the same number of seedlings sprouted.
choices.C: Tray 2 had fewer seedlings sprouted than Tray 1.
choices.D: The number of seedlings sprouted decreased from Tray 1 to Tray 4.

explanation: Tray 4 had 20 seedlings sprouted, more than the other trays.

prompt:
Jonah used to rush through his drawings, filling a page quickly and moving on. In art class, his teacher asked him to spend ten minutes looking closely at a single leaf before sketching it. At first, Jonah felt impatient, but soon he noticed tiny veins and uneven edges he had never paid attention to before.
Which choice best describes what happens in the text?

choices.A: Jonah learns that careful observation can change how he draws.
choices.B: Jonah decides to stop drawing leaves because they are too difficult.
choices.C: Jonah proves that quick sketches are always more accurate.
choices.D: Jonah teaches his art teacher a new drawing method.

explanation: Jonah first rushes through drawings but then notices new details after observing carefully.

prompt:
In a passage about early radio broadcasting, a writer explains that live programs sometimes included unexpected pauses, mistakes, or background sounds. The writer adds, “These imperfections can make old recordings feel less polished than modern broadcasts, but they also remind listeners that the programs were created in real time.”
What is the main function of the quoted sentence?

choices.A: It explains how flaws in old radio recordings can reveal something about how the programs were made.
choices.B: It argues that modern broadcasts should include more mistakes and pauses.
choices.C: It lists the types of equipment used in early radio studios.
choices.D: It shows that old radio programs were never performed live.

explanation: The quoted sentence says imperfections show that early programs were created in real time.

prompt:
The city’s winter festival includes music, food vendors, and ice sculptures. ______ visitors can take free walking tours of historic buildings downtown.

explanation: The second sentence adds another festival activity to the list.

prompt:

explanation: “Each” is singular, so it requires the singular verb “has.”

prompt:
The poem was written by Joy Harjo, ______ former US poet laureate whose work often draws on memory, music, and history.

prompt:
The volunteers divided the supplies among ______ before carrying the boxes into the gym.

explanation: The reflexive pronoun “themselves” correctly indicates that the volunteers divided the supplies among their own group.

prompt:

• The axolotl is a salamander native to lakes near Mexico City.
• Unlike many amphibians, axolotls can remain aquatic throughout their lives.
• Axolotls can regrow lost limbs and some damaged tissues.
• Scientists study axolotls to learn more about regeneration.
• Wild axolotl populations have declined because of habitat loss and pollution.

choices.A: The axolotl is a salamander native to lakes near Mexico City.
choices.B: Because axolotls can regrow lost limbs and some damaged tissues, scientists study them to learn more about regeneration.
choices.C: Wild axolotl populations have declined because of habitat loss and pollution.
choices.D: Unlike many amphibians, axolotls can remain aquatic throughout their lives.

explanation: This choice explains the feature that makes axolotls scientifically interesting.

prompt:
The cookbook includes detailed instructions for beginners. ______ it offers a glossary that explains unfamiliar cooking terms.
Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
explanation: The glossary is another feature that helps beginners, so “Similarly” is logical.

prompt:

prompt:

prompt:
Community repair cafés invite people to bring broken household items, such as lamps or small appliances, to a shared workspace. Volunteers help owners identify problems and make repairs when possible. These events can reduce waste while also helping people learn basic repair skills.

prompt:
Biologists studying monarch butterflies have found that the insects migrate long distances between breeding areas and wintering sites. The butterflies use environmental cues, including the position of the sun, to help guide their journey.

choices.B: The ability to live entirely underwater
choices.D: Sounds made by other insect species

explanation: The text states that monarch butterflies use environmental cues, including the sun’s position, to guide migration.

prompt:
